text:
marta: Heads-up — poke on console routing editor for tiers. UX currently forces hard quota only and the policy editor hides fallbacks. We need a preview that shows where requests will land (region + variant) and what happens when quota is hit.
andrea: Agreed. We keep getting support tickets where free-tier hits burst and silently gets downgraded to a slower variant, customers think its a model change.
kevin: Can we add a column in the routing preview: primary_variant / fallback_variant / fallback_reason? simple table view based on sample inputs.
owen: proposal: expose both soft_quota and hard_quota in policy schema. soft_quota triggers a routed fallback with a TTL grace_window and emits telemetry, hard_quota denies or throttles. soft_quota should be honored only for free/pro, enterprise default to no soft fallback.
andrea: Nice. UX question — where do we show the grace_window? in the policy editor next to quota fields and in the route preview timeline. Also need inline help text: "soft quota = prefer lower-cost variant before blocking"
kevin: Implementation note: internal routing API could add /v1/route/preview that accepts {tenant_id, sample_requests, policy_version} and returns deterministic decisions + telemetry_estimates (p95 latency, cost_per_1k). That lets console show per-request expected outcome.
marta: +1 for preview endpoint. We should gate preview to authenticated console users only (no public API). Also need to ensure preview respects pinning/overrides.
ci-bot: deploy:preview-service started for routing-preview on staging -> logs: https://staging-ci.company/routing-preview/3456
andrea: On enforcement: rather than immediate hard fail, could we soft-debt where requests after hard_quota get a short 429-with-retry-after and a signal to ops? Ops wants an alert when fallback_rate > 5% for 5m.
owen: Telemetry additions: fallback_rate, fallback_latency_delta (fallback_p95 - primary_p95), soft_quota_evictions, revenue_impact_estimate. Make them taggable by tier and region.
kevin: Also we should add a header in routed responses: X-Redwood-Route: variant=redwood-v1; fallback=none; reason=policy-match so customers can debug. For fallbacks X-Redwood-Route: variant=redwood-quantized-v1; fallback=soft-quota; reason=soft_quota_reduction
marta: Good. Thinking about rollout UX: when we flip soft_quota default on for free tier, we should canary it to 10% free tenants and run a daily diff: quality_regressions vs cost_savings tagged by tenant. console should expose that diff.
andrea: Can we bake an eval set into preview? e.g., upload 20 representative prompts per tenant to simulate quality_pre/post. Might be heavy but useful for enterprise.
owen: Implementation caveat: batching and KV cache means predicted latency for mixed variants is tricky. routing-preview should model KV-warm vs KV-cold assumptions. docs must say: "estimates are approximations".
kevin: API shape suggestion: policy object example in editor: ```json
{
  "tier": "free",
  "quota": {"soft": 100000, "hard": 120000, "window_secs": 3600, "grace_window_secs": 600},
  "fallback": [{"when":"soft_quota","variant":"redwood-quantized-v1","priority":10}],
  "rollout": {"canary_pct":10, "target_tenants": []}
}
```
andrea: Love that. For console we should default soft_quota=null for enterprise and make soft_quota opt-in per tenant.
marta: Next steps: kevin -> sketch preview API and response payloads; andrea -> UX mock for quota editor with inline preview pane; owen -> telemetry metric names and tagging plan; i'll coordinate canary list and rollout ops. Anyone want to own the header change?
kevin: I can add header change + routing-preview API in the same PR.
owen: i'll write the metric docs and alert rule drafts.
andrea: i'll mock the editor tomorrow and add copy for help text.
ci-bot: ci:build 7825 passed (routing-preview service)
marta: thanks all. Filing a quick follow-up ticket for product to collect sample eval sets from a couple enterprise customers before canary.
